body: Why SAMPLER_NEAREST_CLAMP or is that the 0 previously?

The shaders now use only one sampler for the textures, which are now provided simply as a static array of texture2d. I followed the example from the scene shader, where this approach is used for lightmaps for example

I would have expected SAMPLER_FILTER_LINEAR because the aliased pixels is worse than blurry, according to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyquist%E2%80%93Shannon_sampling_theorem

```
<constant name="SAMPLER_FILTER_NEAREST" value="0" enum="SamplerFilter">
	Nearest-neighbor sampler filtering. Sampling at higher resolutions than the source will result in a pixelated look.
</constant>
<constant name="SAMPLER_FILTER_LINEAR" value="1" enum="SamplerFilter">
	Bilinear sampler filtering. Sampling at higher resolutions than the source will result in a blurry look.
</constant>
```

Ah, in that case nearest sampling has also been used previously, the sampler just used to be bound to the texture. For rendering on a mesh, it's true that linear is objectively better, but in this case the compute shader needs the exact pixels at a specified coordinate
That is a satisfactory explanation. Thanks!
